transcript.text: Welcome to On Print Shop.
In this tutorial we'll explore the new Adaptive Size Templates feature.
With this update, creating and managing templates becomes much easier and more flexible.
Until now, every template had to be created separately for each product size.
This was time consuming and often meant duplicating the same design multiple times.
The new feature changes that by allowing you to create a single free size template that can be assigned to multiple products.
This saves time, reduces duplication, and improves efficiency.
To support this, a new option called Template Option has been added.
When you create a template here, you can choose either specific product, which works the same as before, or adaptive size, which lets you design a template without linking it to a product right away.
Selecting the Adaptive size option opens up more flexibility.
You can choose from preset size ratio such as square, landscape or portrait, or define your own custom size by entering width and height manually.
This option is available for customizable templates in standard products and photo books.
As you set up your template, you can also define the number of pages, add a group name for easier assignment later, and then continue directly to the designer studio to create your design.
From here, the template behaves just like a regular one, except it remains independent of any product until you decide to assign it.
After creating a template, the next step is to assign it to products.
From the template listing screen, open the Action menu and click Assign to Products.
On this screen, you can assign templates by selecting a product category or by choosing specific products and reviewing their available sizes.
To guide you in selecting the right fit, the system uses color codes, green for a perfect match, yellow for a near match, and red for sizes that don't align well.
This makes it easy to confidently assign templates where they fit best.
You can either manually select product sizes or use the quick filter at the top right corner to assign in one click.
With this filter, you can choose to assign the template to all sizes, only, perfect matches, partial matches, or no match sizes.
Once your selections are made, the assigned product sizes will be displayed and you can save this configuration for future use.
For example, let's save this selection as Minimalist.
Once saved, you'll notice a new drop down called Save Selection, making it easier to reapply your saved product size choices in future assignments.
In addition, Adaptive Size templates can also be assigned in bulk using the new Template assignment option.

Here you can choose either specific product, which works the same way as before, or Adaptive Size, where you can select a template group, filter by category, pick specific products, apply saved selections, and review size matches.
This makes template assignment more flexible, faster, and highly efficient on the storefront.
When customers open a template in the designer studio, it automatically adjusts to the size they choose in the price calculator or defaults to the product size if none is selected.
The template always keeps its original orientation and can be fully personalized with images, clip art, and backgrounds.
With adaptive size templates, template creation is smarter and faster.
It gives admins more flexibility in managing designs while providing customers with more options to choose from.
This new feature saves time, reduces duplication, and ensures A smoother design experience.
Thank you for watching this tutorial.
If you have any questions, our support executives are here to help.
Just reach out through live chat on onprintshop.com.
Thanks for tuning in.

Customizable: These are templates that users can personalize using the Design Studio before placing an order.
Non-Customizable: Pre-designed templates that users cannot edit or modify. They are ready-to-use designs where only the fixed content is printed.
PDF Block: These templates are customizable within the HTML Studio instead of the Design Studio. They use editable blocks in the PDF format.
Upload Print Ready PDF: These are pre-designed PDFs that admins can upload and use as templates, but they cannot be customized within the system.
Template Layouts: A predefined page structure is used to create multiple templates with a consistent layout. This helps maintain design uniformity across various print products.
